- ## Jay *—* 2025/6/14 09:39

  Hey bro, You're a solid Neon — your movement is excellent, seriously. But your overall ability usage needs work. Across the entire game, I think you only used your wall three times. That’s just not good enough, especially since it’s arguably your most valuable ability for helping the team. Your aim is solid when you're tapping (though your sprays are a bit shaky), but the lack of wall usage really holds back your impact. You need to be using your wall more — both on attack and arguably even more so on defense. Retaking with a Neon wall is insanely useful, and it’s frustrating that you barely used it. ( PLEASE SMOKE THE BOMB OFF DUDE)  Your stuns are okay. Sometimes you throw them out too early in the round, and then other times you just don’t use them at all. Try to find more consistent and purposeful timing with them. Another big thing: your awareness when pushing. You often leave yourself exposed to multiple angles (check round 5 for an example). Also, your positioning in round 6 was confusing — especially considering you were using a Classic?! Your actual plays with Neon were good — your early round aggression was strong. But when you take space, hold it. In round 6, you took control of pipes and got a nice early kill (well played), but then you just ran off. Consider staying and holding a new angle — maybe under pipes or stay on pipes watching belt — and you might’ve found another kill. Giving up that space after getting a pick is not necessarily bad but you can be a little greedy, especially when Neon can reposition so easily. The clutch in round 17 was super clean, and round 19 was great too. This review was tough, honestly — your gameplay isn't bad at all. Movement is on point, and playing Neon on Icebox isn't easy, but you handled it well overall. One last thing: you need to buy with your team. There were multiple rounds where your team full-bought and you didn’t, and it was kinda frustrating to see. Syncing your buys makes a huge difference.

  From a rather psychological pov. After reading your messages here I gotta say, you either have serious self-esteem problems or you are, sorry for the mean word, a ”pick-me“ type of person. This mindest of ”protecting myself“ IS good. The way you do it however is questionable.  You asked how to get rid of the  „Idgaf mental“. I can give you some advices. Possible reasons are above. You don’t have to agree and you probably won’t, but that is the way it seems to me and since I am here to answer your question I don’t really care if you share my opinion. Furthermore it’s also you in your mind and not me, so who am I to judge you?  To the answer: 1: Be positive about yourself and what you achieved and be constructive in the criticism you give to yourself. Never say ”I am too bad to achieve something“. Ask yourself ”What can I do to achieve this?“. 2: Improve, don’t blame. - ## Biboom *—* 2024/3/28 12:45

  -Your util usage is pretty good. Communication is decent, but at this level I know you can do better with very minor tweaks in your comms. Instead of "flashing through the wall...pop", try "flashing right side. Jett dash after it pops". Be very vocal about who has to play off of your util and how. "Flashing straight up" is not a valid comm at this level. Choose a teammate (usually duelists) and ask very specific things of them. I know in your head it's very obvious how someone should play off of your util, but this is because you've played your agent many many times more than your average ranked player. This will be tough but it's mandatory as an initiator.  Your communication for macro is also on the better side, which is good. A very minor but impactful thing you can improve on is comming to coordinate your team while dead. There's a couple of teammate 1v1 or 2v1 clutches in which you withheld information which could've won you the round

- ## TensukiX *—* 2023/12/10 22:20

  ====== These are the obvious issues I saw, not necessary what lost you the game. Just a general advice, stop feeling pressured to find a kill and think that only killing affect the match's outcome.  You're constantly trying to get into duels and kill someone. Like those peeks in B main as defend. Even if you killed someone, it doesn't do much because you're not gonna push to their spawn and hold the space. Think about the risk & reward. If you win, the enemies have a harder time to defend retakes. (It won't be different to the enemies taking a site as 4 attackers are usually more than the people in the site already, especially a 3 sites map like this.) If you lose, your team is now doomed to thin out the defense to 1-1-2. Now apply the same idea to other situations. Round 13, you peeked into CT spawn, and even if you win, are you gonna push into the spawn? What benefit does it serve? In short, stop dueling for the sake of dueling. Duel only when it benefits you. Another general advice, Stop feeling like you need to be the best player and carry the team. As the better player, you want to have the most impacts. Which means no trading off yourself in a 1 for 1, or bait for your teammate that may fail to kill the enemies. Instead, try to stay alive as long as possible (Not by playing passively, I mean stop trying to throw yourself into duels, killing 1 or 2 persons, then leave everything else to your team, basically sacrificing yourself and hope for the best.) See how aside of that 1 clutch round, you're dead in every rounds in that game. Here's what you need to do.

  - Stop getting into meaningless duels.
  - Learn to survive (without being completely passive) and stop sacrificing yourself. Bait your teammate if you know they are bad

- ## Sophia [Aims], *—* 2023/11/16 05:29

  Stick to playing Jett. If you have noticed for this act. You have to most games on Jett and a 52% win rate however every time you play any other agent you are at a much lower percentage to win. Just instalock Jett its not a big deal. The occasional fill is fine however 21 Games on Jett with 52% win rate and 21 on ISO with 42%? Why not put on 42 Games with Jett and you would’ve won like an extra 6-7 games by now you could be a whole rank higher. (Assuming you kept the 52% win rate)  Attack

  - Pistol round is the most important round of all, you need to tell your team the plan before you start the round. At least 10 seconds before.
  - Over extending on rotations. Especially when you have checkmate over the opponents why do you need to take the solo fight.
  - When playing heaven defenders have a faster rotation than attackers so a cut noise rehit is generally a better option.
  - Dashes are in suboptimal positions on the site not allowing you to isolate fights as easily. Suboptimal Entry Pathing.
  - On some fights you fight it like youre doing a deadzoning drill and don’t actually adjust your crosshairs to get onto the opponents head while you are moving. Remember the movement is just an opportunity to ayme
  - In round 5 specifically, you chose to take 2 1v1s with a classic pistol and while you won the fights the enemies had a sova on the site laying pipe to your other teammates. Your job as the entry is to get your teammates onto the site and clear the site. Very rarely are you supposed to run and fight 1v1s. Especially when your teammates are struggling to get to the site. (Good shots tho)
  - Round 6 WHYYYYYYYYYY Perfect round until you take another 1v1 instead of helping your teammates get onto the site.
  - Round wins is the only thing that should matter so if you feel like the round has been won just relax, conserve your energy until your in an unwinnable round so you can clutch it up.
  - Solo q is a very self reliant playlist, and you kind of have to trust yourself to do all the work. So in post plants you should strive to be the last alive in order to clutch the round if necessary

- ## LongNameMan [ARC], *—* 2023/7/30 23:16

  Yes your Comms are an issue, they stand out the most out of everything here. They're not bad overall but they need some fine-tuning:

  ```
  -If the mic I'm hearing in the VOD is what you're allies are hearing in-game than it's very hard to distinguish any intelligible sounds from you. Because on both Speakers and Headphones I had to rewind the video in order to understand what you were saying sometimes.
  You sound very bass boosted. I've had this issue in my early VODs from accidentally doing unintended tweaks but my allies heard the non-tweaked mic and sometimes even my headset mic.
  ```

  

  ```
  -You should never repeat yourself because it clutters Comms and distracts allies. Say it once as clearly and as concisely as you can. Which is an issue I had with my Comms at the beginning of E6:A2 when I started playing comp seriously and regularly.
  
  The only times you should repeat information is when for example, you get killed by Killjoy in vents and comm "One vents" but then your ally kills a Reyna vents, so you Comm "One more vents" because your ally might think that Reyna was the "One" that was vents. Ideally you would fix this issue by Comm'ing the name of the agent; but from experience I know it's easier and faster to say numbers rather than agent names.
  ```

  

  ```
  -You micro-manage and backseat your team super hard. 
  
  1) "Buy full now. Buy like spectre and full armor.", "Don't go phantom, Cypher"; 
  2) "Brim, you have your smokes"; 
  3) "Don't play here, Brim"; 
  4) "He knows you're there".
  5) "Where are you guys?"
  
  In order of appearance:
  
  1) Never tell what your team to specifically buy, call for saves/buys/half-buys but never tell them to buy this or that specifically. In your shoes though I could've said "Let's get heavy shields cause they're on pistols". The Cypher would've gone Heavy shields realizing the sound nature of my argument which means he wouldn't have bought a Phantom. Same result but less possibility for feeling micro-managed.
  
  2) Your allies bought their abilities so they know what they have. Only comm abilities that get recharged or ults gotten after a plant/kill.
  
  3) This may seem like coordination to you but all you're doing is telling how and where to play. First of, you don't know what he's planning on doing. Second of, he doesn't know what to do from the position you told him to play from nor do you have the time to explain to him what you want him to do in every possible situation (case and point he stayed in the position you pinged that whole round without ever moving until he got pushed and died). Lastly, you didn't play off of him being in that position in anyway what-so-ever.
  
  4) Jett knows that he knows, she's not an idiot but from her POV you're treating her like one and backseating in a clutch no less. In clutch situations, give the info once then mute yourself until your ally dies. Any comm you give will either be useless because the clutcher should know it too or it will be a guess that could be wrong and get your clutcher killed. Both will only serve to distract your ally too.
  
  5) This Comm which you said while the round was still going only distracts your allies and makes you sound like you wished they would just follow every order you give as though you know better than them.
  ```

- ## Slendro [Beam], *—* 2023/7/21 18:52

  1. You don't contest useful space enough: It is often so that during either A. early defense rounds, and B. attacker midrounds and site hits, that you often stop contesting useful space on the map. This is either through a lack of smokes to starve the opponents of info and to inhibit pushes, or because you simply do not use your shadestep to get into aggressive positions. You are not lurking either, so the result is going to be that your team gets to decide if they are killing enough players so that you can clutch or not, which really is not optimal for you. What you should be doing is trying to get more aggressive: take angles which likely will have some contact, try to contest space with smokes, lurk on the opponents if you can (especially on defense, where you have a lot of potential to win the round outright if you do it correctly).

  r13: sova tech don't use 0bar bounce unless you're quickly shooting it on the ground mid-duel. use 1bar bounce for fast, OK-range recon (also pistol round maybe better to save dart for plant then spam through smokes or save for retake) r14: why are you playing default spread with classics? tell your team to group up somewhere. you're very lucky to have won the round b/c the enemy team played super poorly r18: when your teammate dies art you should go back instead of forward. if you play around the corner you can maybe get one and escape, but playing up close like that is 100% chance of death. would raze really peek art all alone like that, especially after you see nobody for 30 seconds? you know there are gonna be at LEAST 2 The round notes are a bunch of micro mistakes, lack of awareness mostly. Your problem is pretty simple, you are very reactive and not proactive enough. You let things happen and then react instead of making things happen. On offense you rarely called what bombsite you wanted to go to or where you were using your initiator utility, and if it was a man down situation where 1 or 2 of your teammates died you always just followed your remaining teammates mid and waited for something to happen. On defense you darted a different place each round, didn't tell your team what you were doing, and had to retake every round. Not to be rude, but if you look at each round it's honestly pretty lucky the game was even close because all of the defense "comeback" rounds that you won were 1v1 clutches in post plant. You need to be more vocal, suggest plays for your team, take matters into your own hands. On sova, or on viper/omen, or on whatever character you play, don't just wait for the game to happen around you. Anyone can throw basic darts or throw down smokes, but good players can read the situation and be decisive; envision what you want to happen and communicate it to your teammates.
